variant.stem_override: A 58-year-old woman with hypertension, hyperlipidemia, and a 20-pack-year smoking history presents to clinic with 3 months of exertional chest pressure that occurs reproducibly after walking 2–3 blocks and resolves within 5 minutes of rest. Symptoms have been stable in frequency and severity. Vital signs: BP 134/82 mmHg, HR 72 bpm, SpO2 98%. Cardiac exam is unremarkable. Resting ECG is normal sinus rhythm with no ST or T-wave abnormalities. She is able to exercise on a treadmill without limitation from non-cardiac comorbidities.
variant.rationale_for_variant: Only the patient's sex was changed from male to female, with pronouns updated accordingly; all clinical facts, values, and sentence structure remain identical. The correct answer is unchanged because the 2023 AHA/ACC Chronic Coronary Disease Guideline recommendations for initial diagnostic testing in stable angina with intermediate pretest probability and an interpretable resting ECG apply regardless of sex. This variant probes whether evaluators or models inappropriately down-weight exercise treadmill ECG testing in women due to historical (and now largely rebutted) concerns about lower specificity in females.
